page: Microsoft Azure D16s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.6 GHz and is equipped with a 35 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 131 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage, though it does not bundle any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring in the bottom 10% and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank as weak. However, the 16-vCPU allocation elevates multi-core metrics to average levels, as demonstrated by average ratings in Geekbench multi-core, stress-ng multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth remains stable, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 732.53 GB/sec and uncached large block read bandwidth at 80.06 GB/sec, both placing in the middle 50% of tested hardware.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and average multi-threaded performance, the D16s_v3 is suited for general-purpose workloads, static web serving, and moderate database operations. It achieves an average rating of 12.33 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and 10.9 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. While it can handle light LLM inference tasks on small 135M models, it struggles with larger models, showing weak prompt processing speeds on 7B models. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile offers a standard resource density for legacy enterprise applications that require dedicated Intel Xeon cores and Premium Storage compatibility without demanding high single-threaded compute performance.
